title: Fractional COO for Owner-Led Businesses | Vestis Solutions
description: A fractional COO for owner-led trade and service businesses. Fix the processes, roles and weekly rhythm so the business runs without you in every decision.
h1: A fractional COO for owners who are still the bottleneck
intro: Every question still comes to you. Jobs slip, follow-ups get missed, and the crew waits on your answer before they move. You want a business that runs on a plan, not on your phone, and a fractional COO can help you build it.
definition: A fractional COO is a part-time chief operating officer who works with a business a few hours a month to fix how work gets done: processes, roles, handoffs and the weekly meeting rhythm. You get operations leadership without hiring a full-time executive.

sections.h2: What a fractional COO fixes first
paras: Most owner-led companies don't have a people problem. They have a handoff problem. A lead comes in, a quote goes out, a job gets scheduled, and somewhere in between, things fall through because nobody owns the step.
I start by walking through how work actually moves in your business, from first call to final invoice. Then we pick the one bottleneck that costs you the most and fix that first.
bullets: Who owns each step, written down so it holds when you're not there
A simple weekly meeting with the numbers you actually watch
Clear roles before you hire, so the next person knows their job
Your existing tools connected, so the team stops entering the same data twice

sections.h2: Why a part-time COO instead of a full-time hire
paras: A full-time COO is a big salary for a company that may need ten or twelve focused hours a month. A part-time COO gives you the outside view and the structure, and you keep the cash for crews, trucks and marketing.
It also lowers the risk. If the fit is wrong, you haven't made a six-figure hire you can't undo.

You get four 30-minute owner sessions a month, plus support between calls, and up to 12 delivery hours for meetings, implementation and support. The first 90 days go like this: we find the bottleneck, fix it one piece at a time, and review what changed every 30 days. After that, it's month to month.

Operations is one part of the work. The same partnership covers getting found on Google and in AI answers, and a review of your sales process, because more leads on a broken process only means more stress.

For over a decade I worked in banking and finance with business owners through cash crunches, growing pains and big wins. Then I co-founded a company with a partner and lived it myself. I'm based in Charlotte, NC, and work with owner-led businesses locally and across the US.

faq.q: What does a fractional COO do?
faq.a: A fractional COO fixes how the work gets done in your business, part time. That means mapping your processes, deciding who owns each step, setting up a weekly meeting with clear numbers, and holding the team to it. The goal is a business that keeps moving when the owner isn't answering every question.

faq.q: How much does a fractional COO cost?
faq.a: Fractional COO pricing varies widely by scope and hours. My partnerships start at $3,000 a month, which includes operations help along with SEO and AEO, a sales process review, and four owner sessions. You see the number before anything starts, and nothing outside the agreed scope goes ahead without your approval.

faq.q: Is a fractional COO worth it for a small business?
faq.a: It is worth it when you, the owner, are the bottleneck and a full-time COO salary doesn't make sense yet. You get structure and an outside view for a fraction of a full-time hire. If your processes already run well without you, you probably don't need one.

faq.q: What is the difference between a fractional COO and a consultant?
faq.a: A consultant usually delivers a report, while a fractional COO stays in the work with you month after month. I meet with you every week, help your team put changes in place, and review results every 30 days. The point is a fix that sticks, not a plan that sits in a drawer.

faq.q: How long do you work with a fractional COO?
faq.a: Most owners start with a set period and then continue as needed. I start with 90 days, which is long enough to fix something real and measure it. After that, we continue month to month, so you stay because it's working, not because a contract says so.

faq.q: Can a fractional COO work remotely?
faq.a: Yes, most of the work happens on video calls and inside your existing tools. I'm based in Charlotte, NC, and work with owner-led businesses both locally and remotely across the US. Owner sessions, team meetings and process reviews all work well over video.
